title: Make the case for a product team
prompt: Northwind's VP of Product will fund a permanent design system team only if you show evidence that the company needs one. Which of these findings support funding the system **as a product with a standing team**? Select every one that applies.
hints: Look for evidence of ongoing, repeated cost, not a one-time problem.
Ask of each finding: would a one-quarter cleanup project fix it for good?
explanation: Forked components, 64 greys and a steady stream of requests are all symptoms of a shared need with no owner. A one-off project would fix them once and then watch them return. A single app with a single team, or a launch announcement, is not evidence of a cross-team need.

forks.text: Six teams have copied the 2021 Button into their own repos to fix bugs locally.
forks.why: Correct. Forks prove teams need shared components but have nobody upstream to fix them, which is an ownership problem.

greys.text: The audit found 64 distinct grey values across the dispatch app and marketing site.
greys.why: Correct. Drift at this scale comes from many teams making the same decision independently, again and again.

one-app.text: The dispatch app's own team wants to rename its CSS classes.
one-app.why: That's one team's internal refactor; it doesn't need a shared system or a dedicated team.

requests.text: Every month, about five teams ask in Slack whether a date picker or data table already exists.
requests.why: Correct. Recurring demand from many teams is exactly the user base a product team serves.

launch.text: Leadership wants a design system announcement for the company all-hands next month.
launch.why: A launch date is a project milestone; it says nothing about the ongoing need that justifies a permanent team.
